A young white rhinoceros calf, typically unsteady for the first few days.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/White_rhino_female_and_young_grazing.webm/250px--White_rhino_female_and_young_grazing.webm.jpg)](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c3/White_rhino_female_and_young_grazing.webm/White_rhino_female_and_young_grazing.webm.480p.vp9.webm)

A white rhino female with her calf grazing in [Pilanesberg National Park](/wiki/Pilanesberg_National_Park "Pilanesberg National Park").

Females (cows) typically reach sexual maturity between six and seven years of age, whereas males (bulls) mature later, usually between 10 and 12 years. Courtship among white rhinos is often a prolonged and sometimes arduous affair. A persistent bull will often stay near a cow even when she acts aggressively, emitting calls as he approaches. He may chase or block the cow's path, vocalizing with loud squeals or wails if she attempts to leave his territory. When a cow is ready to mate, she signals her receptiveness by curling her tail and adopting a rigid stance during the copulation, which lasts about half an hour.[[40]](#cite_note-41) Breeding pairs may remain together for 5 to 20 days before separating.

fanoutqa_036644.x:
France national football team :: Competitive record :: UEFA European Championship :: part 01 :: chunk_0031
Main article: [France at the UEFA European Championship](/wiki/France_at_the_UEFA_European_Championship "France at the UEFA European Championship")

France is one of the most successful nations at the [UEFA European Championship](/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") having won two titles in [1984](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1984 "UEFA Euro 1984") and [2000](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2000 "UEFA Euro 2000"). The team is just below [Spain](/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") with four titles and [Germany](/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") with three. France hosted the [inaugural competition](/wiki/1960_European_Nations%27_Cup "1960 European Nations' Cup") in 1960 and have appeared in eleven UEFA European Championship tournaments, tied for fourth-best. The team won their first title on home soil in 1984 and were led by [Ballon d'Or](/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or "Ballon d'Or") winner [Michel Platini](/wiki/Michel_Platini "Michel Platini"). In 2000, the team, led by [FIFA World Player of the Year](/wiki/FIFA_World_Player_of_the_Year "FIFA World Player of the Year") Zinedine Zidane, won its second title in Belgium and the Netherlands. The team's worst result in the competition was a first-round elimination in [1992](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1992 "UEFA Euro 1992") and [2008](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008").

fanoutqa_006948.x:
List of states and union territories of India by population :: part 03 :: chunk_0002
[India](/wiki/India "India") is a union consisting of [28 states and 8 union territories](/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India").[[1]](#cite_note-official-1) As of 2024, with an estimated population of 1.484 [billion](/wiki/1,000,000,000 "1,000,000,000"), India is the [world's most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"). India occupies 2.4% of the [world's area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area") and is home to 17.5% of the [world's population](/wiki/World_population "World population").[[2]](#cite_note-2) The [Indo-Gangetic Plain](/wiki/Indo-Gangetic_Plain "Indo-Gangetic Plain") has one of the world's biggest stretches of fertile not-deep [alluvium](/wiki/Alluvium "Alluvium") and are among the most densely populated areas of the world. The [eastern](/wiki/Eastern_Coastal_Plains "Eastern Coastal Plains") and [western](/wiki/Western_Coastal_Plains "Western Coastal Plains") coastal regions of [Deccan Plateau](/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") are also densely populated regions of India. The [Thar Desert](/wiki/Thar_Desert "Thar Desert") in western Rajasthan is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.[[3]](#cite_note-3) The northern and [north-eastern states](/wiki/Northeast_India "Northeast India") along the [Himalayas](/wiki/Himalayas "Himalayas") contain cold arid deserts with fertile valleys. These states have relatively low population density due to indomitable physical barriers.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Kleiman, born in 1988, was raised in the [Lincoln Park](/wiki/Lincoln_Park,_Chicago "Lincoln Park, Chicago") neighborhood of Chicago as a [Chicago Bulls](/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") fan. He attended the [University of Chicago Laboratory Schools](/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Laboratory_Schools "University of Chicago Laboratory Schools") graduating from the High School in 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Kleiman attended the [University of Southern California](/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California") majoring in psychology from 2006 to 2010. During this time, he served as a public relations intern for the [Los Angeles Lakers](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") and joined the [Delta Tau Delta](/wiki/Delta_Tau_Delta "Delta Tau Delta") fraternity.

In 2013, Kleiman earned his [J.D.](/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from [Duke University School of Law](/wiki/Duke_University_School_of_Law "Duke University School of Law").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

During the [2012-13 season](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_NBA_season "2012–13 NBA season"), Kleiman was a basketball operations intern for the [Charlotte Bobcats](/wiki/Charlotte_Bobcats "Charlotte Bobcats") under general manager [Rich Cho](/wiki/Rich_Cho "Rich Cho").

Main article: [Religion in Africa](/wiki/Religion_in_Africa "Religion in Africa")

See also: [African divination](/wiki/African_divination "African divination")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Religion_distribution_Africa_crop.png/330px-Religion_distribution_Africa_crop.png)](/wiki/File:Religion_distribution_Africa_crop.png)

A map showing religious distribution in Africa

While Africans profess a wide variety of religious beliefs, the majority of the people respect African religions or parts of them. However, in formal surveys or census, most people will identify with major religions that came from outside the continent, mainly through colonisation. There are several reasons for this, the main one being the colonial idea that African religious beliefs and practices are not good enough. Religious beliefs and statistics on religious affiliation are difficult to come by since they are often a sensitive topic for governments with mixed religious populations.[[245]](#cite_note-Stanford-259)[[246]](#cite_note-NYT-260) According to the *[World Book Encyclopedia](/wiki/World_Book_Encyclopedia "World Book Encyclopedia")*, [Islam](/wiki/Islam_in_Africa "Islam in Africa") and [Christianity](/wiki/Christianity_in_Africa "Christianity in Africa") are the two largest religions in Africa. Islam is most prevalent in Northern Africa, and is the state religion of many North African countries, such as Algeria, where 99% of the population practices Islam.[[247]](#cite_note-261) The majority of people in most governments in Southern, Southeast, and Central Africa, as well as in a sizable portion of the Horn of Africa and West Africa, identify as [Christians](/wiki/Christians "Christians"). The NBA retired [Bill Russell](/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell")'s No. 6 for all its member teams on August 11, 2022.[[68]](#cite_note-68)[[69]](#cite_note-69)

James K. Polk :: Post-presidency and death (1849) :: chunk_0033
[![A marble tomb, with four columns supporting a roof](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/James_Polk_Grave.jpg/250px-James_Polk_Grave.jpg)](/wiki/File:James_Polk_Grave.jpg)

James K. Polk's tomb lies on the grounds of the [Tennessee State Capitol](/wiki/Tennessee_State_Capitol "Tennessee State Capitol")

Polk's time in the White House took its toll on his health. Full of enthusiasm and vigor when he entered office, Polk left the presidency exhausted by his years of public service.[[246]](#cite_note-249) He left Washington on March 6 for a pre-arranged triumphal tour of the [Southern United States](/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States"), to end in Nashville.[[247]](#cite_note-250) Polk had two years previously arranged to buy a house there, afterwards dubbed [Polk Place](/wiki/Polk_Place "Polk Place"), that had once belonged to his mentor, Felix Grundy.[[248]](#cite_note-251)

James and Sarah Polk progressed down the Atlantic coast, and then westward through the [Deep South](/wiki/Deep_South "Deep South"). He was enthusiastically received and banqueted. By the time the Polks reached Alabama, he was suffering from a bad cold, and soon became concerned by reports of [cholera](/wiki/Cholera "Cholera")—a passenger on Polk's [riverboat](/wiki/Riverboat "Riverboat") died of it, and it was rumored to be common in New Orleans, but it was too late to change plans. Worried about his health, he would have departed the city quickly but was overwhelmed by Louisiana hospitality. Several passengers on the riverboat up the Mississippi died of the disease, and Polk felt so ill that he went ashore for four days, staying in a hotel. A doctor assured him he did not have cholera, and Polk arrived in Nashville on April 2 to a huge reception.[[249]](#cite_note-252)

[Political parties](/wiki/Political_parties_in_the_United_States "Political parties in the United States") have dominated [American politics](/wiki/Politics_of_the_United_States "Politics of the United States") for most of the nation's history. Though the [Founding Fathers](/wiki/Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States") generally spurned political parties as divisive and disruptive, and their rise had not been anticipated when the U.S. Constitution was drafted in 1787, organized political parties developed in the U.S. in the mid-1790s nonetheless. They evolved from [political factions](/wiki/Political_faction "Political faction"), which began to appear almost immediately after the Federal government came into existence. Those who supported the [Washington administration](/wiki/Presidency_of_George_Washington "Presidency of George Washington") were referred to as "pro-administration" and would eventually form the [Federalist Party](/wiki/Federalist_Party "Federalist Party"), while those in opposition largely joined the emerging [Democratic-Republican Party](/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party "Democratic-Republican Party").[[195]](#cite_note-201)

Greatly concerned about the very real capacity of political parties to destroy the fragile unity holding the nation together, Washington remained [unaffiliated](/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician") with any political faction or party throughout his eight-year presidency. He was, and remains, the only U.S. president never to be affiliated with a political party.[[196]](#cite_note-GWpps-202)[[197]](#cite_note-203) Since Washington, every U.S. president has been affiliated with a political party at the time of assuming office, and, since 1869, every president has been a member of either the [Republican](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") or [Democratic](/wiki/Democr

2013 California wildfires :: Background :: chunk_0001
Further information: [List of California wildfires](/wiki/List_of_California_wildfires "List of California wildfires")

The timing of "fire season" in California is variable, depending on the amount of prior winter and spring precipitation, the frequency and severity of weather such as heat waves and wind events, and moisture content in vegetation. [Northern California](/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California") typically sees wildfire activity between late spring and early fall, peaking in the summer with hotter and drier conditions. Occasional cold frontal passages can bring wind and lightning. The timing of fire season in Southern California is similar, peaking between late spring and fall. The severity and duration of peak activity in either part of the state is modulated in part by weather events: downslope/offshore wind events can lead to critical fire weather, while onshore flow and Pacific weather systems can bring conditions that hamper wildfire growth.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-:02-5)

Below is a list of all fires that exceeded 1,000 acres (400 ha) during the 2013 fire season.[[6]](#cite_note-large-fires-6) The list is taken from [CAL FIRE](/wiki/CAL_FIRE "CAL FIRE")'s list of large fires.

What may have been the most dangerous moment in the crisis was not recognized until the Cuban Missile Crisis Havana conference in October 2002, which marked its 40th anniversary. The three-day conference was sponsored by the private [National Security Archive](/wiki/National_Security_Archive "National Security Archive"), [Brown University](/wiki/Brown_University "Brown University") and the Cuban government[[216]](#cite_note-latinamericanstudies-218) and attended by many of the veterans of the crisis. They learned that on 27 October 1962, a group of eleven United States Navy destroyers and the aircraft carrier [USS *Randolph*](/wiki/USS_Randolph_(CV-15) "USS Randolph (CV-15)") had located a diesel-powered, nuclear-armed Soviet Project 641 (NATO designation [Foxtrot](/wiki/Foxtrot-class_submarine "Foxtrot-class submarine")) submarine, the [*B-59*](/wiki/Soviet_submarine_B-59 "Soviet submarine B-59"), near Cuba. Despite being in international waters, the Americans started dropping practice [depth charges](/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") to attempt to force the submarine to surface.

There had been no contact from Moscow for a number of days and the submarine was running too deep to monitor radio traffic, so those on board did not know whether war had broken out. The captain of the submarine, [Valentin Savitsky](/wiki/Valentin_Savitsky "Valentin Savitsky"), had no way of knowing that the depth charges were non-lethal "practice" rounds, intended as warning shots to force him to surface. Running out of air, the Soviet submarine was surrounded by American warships and desperately needed to surface.
